state:
**Goal `growth-proof`. Stage 5's check should pass on the driver's next sweep. Stage 3 should too.** No floor is carried.

A whole `--iterations --sized` run on this tree found one oversized bench, `core/IO-Metadata/isDir`: both ramps settled at 128. Re-run alone, its ramp was `unclear`, so `--lower` left it, and it was lowered to 256 by hand. A lower N cannot fail the check. Every whole run so far has named a different borderline bench. If the next sweep names another, lower it the same way.

`planBenches` (`tools/nv/proofs/select.ts`) orders the benches a change reaches, runs each one that `benchOrder` puts first and cannot skip, and skips a bench whose changed items are all proven by `PROVEN_BY` (2) benches with no degradation. A degradation unproves the items of the bench that showed it, so every bench sharing one runs, including one passed over before. An item is a changed key in the bench's `Selected.keys`. A bench selected for any other reason (new, red, owed, def, global, diverged) has `items: null` and always runs. `runBenches` judges through it, records only what ran, and passes the skipped ones to `advance` as ran, so each keeps its footprint and verdict. `nv affected --run` prints each skipped bench with its provers and the reached / ran / skipped / red counts. `tools/nv/test/bench-skip.test.ts` holds the four names the Stage 5 check wants. They print only when `CLAUDECODE` is unset, which is how the driver runs it.

Degradation is the growth verdict alone: a rise in the per-operation counts is not compared yet. The provers are printed, not stored in any ledger.

`core/Process-Handle/writeStdin` is a known gap owned by M10. The `unclear` benches do not fail Stage 3's check.

items.text: **Write `## The growth proof` in `docs/perf/performance-pass.md`**: what the proof checks, the bench tree's work before and after Stage 3 (`bun nv scaling --budget`), the reran and skipped counts of one real change's `nv affected --run`, and each bench that needed callgrind or ended unclear, as the goal's `## Stage 6` says. The first `--run` on a machine pays for every bench. Spec: `rule:testing/feature-proofs`, anchor `docs/perf/performance-pass.md:1`.
**`bun nv proofs --gate` owes nothing, growth included**: run it and close what it names. Anchor `tools/nv/cmd/proofs.ts:1`.

backlog: A degradation also counts a rise in a bench's per-operation counts, beside its growth: `runBenches` at `tools/nv/proofs/select.ts` judges growth only (the goal's `## Stage 5`).
The ledger names the benches that proved a skipped bench (the goal's `## Stage 5`): today only `nv affected --run` prints them.
The driver's sweep runs the benches a change reaches: no check holds a bench atom yet.
